title: Blair Atholl to Pitlochry River Garry Walk Route

images.title: Blair Atholl by Ian Taylor, CC BY-SA 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Blair Atholl. Its name derives from the Gaelic 'Blàr Athall,' meaning 'field of Atholl.' The village's growth accelerated in the 19th century with the arrival of the railway in 1863, connecting Perth to Inverness. Blair Atholl is renowned for Blair Castle, a historic landmark that hosts the biennial Blair Atholl International Scout Jamborette, attracting Scouts from around the world. The village also features the Atholl Country Life Museum, showcasing local social history. Additionally, the nearby Blair Athol Distillery in Pitlochry offers guided tours, providing insights into traditional whisky production.

description: This walk or cycle takes you from Blair Atholl to Pitlochry in Perthshire. The walk starts off in the pretty village of Blair Atholl located at the confluence of the Rivers Tilt and Garry. The route then follows trails and country lanes along the River Garry to Killiecrankie. You then continue south to Pitlochry passing the picturesque Linn Of Tummel and Loch Faskally. On the way you can enjoy some fine views of the surrounding mountains of the Caingorms and Scottish Highlands.
